# Conditional transfer to the measured scheduled-memory interface

Date: 2026-10-16. Local mathematical audit; no hardware or threshold claim.

## Verdict

A literal replacement of the partial-boundary theorem's ANY-block-mismatch constant by the new one-node endpoint F_K is false. An exact counterexample is below. There are nevertheless two valid conditional improvements:

1. Complete internal syndrome pinchings, including the successful cuts in the old independent latent-pattern refinement: replace the old capped sum of squared block actions by Q = 1 - product_B cos^2(min(a_B, pi/2)), keeping its ANY-block-mismatch predicate.
2. One scalar full-syndrome partial-pinch node: change the parent predicate to entering-versus-final full-syndrome mismatch, retain actual exact entering and final syndrome pinchings, and use F_K on this new CP refinement. The original REPORT support proof extends to this endpoint-based refinement. This changes the certificate, not the physical channel.

Both need the own-entry/retirement embedding described below. The common-initial-time projector theorem alone is not a proof of either full-input scheduled-memory claim.

## A. Exact obstruction to unchanged-event substitution

Use a memory syndrome qubit with stabilizer Z and an untouched logical spectator. The weak footprint is the syndrome qubit, so its commuting Paulis are I and Z and the full-footprint/no-local-logical condition holds. Enter in |0>, apply U=exp(-i pi X/6), then T=(Id+D_Z)/2, then U, and perform the actual final Z pinching. Correction is identity. All resources may be reserved in one clean parent.

The stipulated channel has its old canonical independent skip/complete-pinch refinement. On a retained middle pinch, the event of at least one block mismatch has probability 1-(3/4)^2=7/16. On a skipped middle pinch, the sole block mismatch probability is sin^2(pi/3)=3/4. Thus the OLD parent event has probability 19/32.

The new binary endpoint formula gives F_1(pi/6,pi/6,1/2)=9/16=18/32. Indeed the actual endpoint mismatch probability is (1/2)(2(1/4)(3/4))+(1/2)(3/4)=18/32. The omitted 1/32 consists of retained-pinch paths that leave and return to the entering syndrome. They are bad in the old event and good in the new endpoint event. Consequently F_1 cannot bound the old event even for a single parent and trivial bath.

This is not a controller, geometry, or logical-e
